meta.regime: The regime has resolved into a single sentence: rising US real rates are beating everything, including a hawkish ECB. The ECB delivered its second hike of the war, revised its own inflation projections UP for 2027 and 2028, and was followed by Reuters sources saying further tightening remains likely - and the euro still fell, because a hot US PPI annual at 5.4% pushed CME FedWatch to 60.6% for September 16 and the cumulative odds of a 2026 hike above 85%. The second feature is the complete collapse of the haven and industrial-metals complex: gold, silver and copper are ALL now negative on the month while crude is +21.39%, so energy is the only asset still paid for the war. The third is that the board has compressed - four currencies sit at +1 and only the yen and the dollar have clean directional cases - which makes the 12:30Z CPI print the single decider for more than half the symbol list.
meta.nextBigEvent: US August CPI TODAY, September 11 at 12:30Z. Consensus is 3.4% headline y/y with +0.4% m/m and core +0.4% m/m at 2.4% y/y; market-implied mean was 3.38% on September 9 and Nowflation carries a 3.36% call. This is the last major data point before the September 16 FOMC and it arrives with CME FedWatch already at 60.6% and the cumulative 2026 hike probability above 85%. Yesterday PPI did the groundwork: headline +0.4% m/m in line but the ANNUAL rate at 5.4% beat by 0.1pp, with energy accounting for more than three quarters of the rise in final-demand goods and diesel up 24.1%, while core PPI came in SOFTER at +0.2% m/m against 0.3% expected. That split is the whole question for today - an energy-driven headline the Fed can look through versus genuine core pass-through. A hot core confirms September 16 and gives the dollar a trend it has not had all month despite DXY at 99.029; a soft core unwinds the 60.6% and hands the bid straight back to gold, silver and the commodity currencies.

dailyRead: Today is a day of consequences rather than surprises, because three things this file wrote down in advance all resolved at once. First, yesterday it said the ECB asymmetry favoured a hawkish surprise and that the staff projections were the entire event. That is exactly what happened: the deposit facility went to 2.50% and the refi to 2.65%, the 2026 inflation forecast was kept at 3.0% but 2027 was revised UP to 2.5% and 2028 to 2.1%, growth was upgraded to 0.9% for 2026 and 1.4% for 2027 on greater-than-expected resilience, Lagarde said inflation risks are tilted to the UPSIDE while growth risks are to the downside, and Reuters sources after the meeting reported further tightening remains LIKELY. The call was right and the euro still FELL, to 1.16116 from 1.16318. That is the single most informative fact on the board: a hawkish ECB lost a head-to-head against the dollar, because US PPI beat on the annual at 5.4% against 5.3% expected and the dollar recovered through the European close. Rising US real rates are not merely beating the war premium, they are now beating another central bank tightening into an energy shock. Second, yesterday named the precise invalidation for short sterling - a hard upside surprise in monthly GDP at 06:00Z. It printed +0.4% m/m against 0.0% expected, accelerating from 0.3% in June, with services +0.4%, production +0.2%, construction +0.1%, annual growth 1.6% and an eighth consecutive three-month period of expansion. The growth leg of the weak-sterling thesis is broken, and so is a second leg that has carried it for three sessions: German gas at 83.14 euros per MWh is +38.65% on the month after a 3.41% session jump, while UK gas at 201.52 pence is +34.03%, so Germany now owns the worst gas exposure in G10 and sterling does not. Two legs in one session is an upgrade, not a footnote: GBP goes from MINUS 1 to ZERO. It does not go positive - the Bank is still frozen at 3.75% with a 0/9 TE vote-cut consensus for September 17, borrowing costs remain the highest in the developed G10, and July government borrowing was 69% above the prior year - but every short-sterling expression is now downgraded and GBP/USD, GBP/AUD and EUR/GBP in particular. Third, yesterday wrote that a second soft copper session would argue for RANGE in XCU/USD and would start to question the Australian score. Copper fell to 6.5049 USD per pound and its MONTHLY return is now NEGATIVE at -1.42%, having been +1.87% yesterday and +2.90% on the week two days ago. Silver is -1.87% on the month and gold -1.11%; all three metals have gone from fading to outright negative while WTI ran to 100.939 and +21.39%. So XCU/USD is downgraded from LONG to RANGE - TE itself now headlines copper holding its decline as tariff fears ease, which removes the front-running bid that sat on top of the genuine physical shortage - and AUD is cut from +2 to +1. The honest statement of that cut: only half the trigger written yesterday was met. Copper had its second soft session, but there was no new weak Australian print today, so this is a one-notch cut rather than a collapse. What forces it is that the commodity leg is now negative rather than merely weak, AUD/USD is -0.44% on the WEEK at 0.71719 with its monthly gain cut from +2.12% to +1.56%, and TE carries consensus AND forecast at 4.35% for September 29 - meaning the rate leg is a static level, not a forward catalyst. Against all of this the yen case got stronger, not weaker, and it is the only score that needs no qualification. The September 1-8 Reuters poll has 97% of 68 economists expecting a hike on September 18, up from 57% in the prior survey; TE now carries consensus AND its own forecast at 1.25%; 89% of analysts see at least 1.50% by end-March and 62% see 1.75% by end-Q2 2027, three months earlier than August; Takata has urged a nimble approach warning overheating risks are rising and Masu said the Bank expects to keep raising to avoid forced rapid tightening later; and 82% of economists said the joint yen-buying intervention and Bessent remarks have lowered the political barrier to hikes. USD/JPY is 154.028, -0.26% today and -3.38% on the month. The dollar is raised to +2 on the PPI beat, 60.6% FedWatch pricing, cumulative 2026 hike odds above 85% from 77% on August 7, a 10-year yield near a 3-year high and that won head-to-head against the ECB - but every dollar-legged conviction is deliberately capped at LOW-MED because August CPI lands at 12:30Z and core PPI came in SOFT at +0.2%. The franc stays at +1 on data and differentials only, with USD/CHF 0.81268 and the haven thesis retired two days ago; note Swiss services PMI fell hard to 58.3 from 63.9. The loonie stays at +1 with USD/CAD 1.38394 and a still-broken oil beta, though CAD is at least +0.73% on the month now. And the kiwi stays at MINUS 1 despite a +0.61% bounce today, because it remains the only major negative on the month at -0.49% and its manufacturing PMI slid again to 53.1 from 54.3. Trade the yen, trade crude, sell the kiwi, short GER40 into the German gas shock - and do not put size on anything with a dollar leg until 12:30Z has printed.

USD.when: Sept 16, 18:00Z - CME FedWatch 60.6% for 25bp to 4.00%, which is also TE's own forecast, with the odds of a hike at some point in 2026 now above 85%
USD.note: TE re-verified this morning: policy rate 3.75% upper bound, CPI 3.4% with MoM 0.1% and core 2.5%, unemployment 4.1%, non-farm payrolls +162,000 against a prior +21,000, average hourly earnings +0.3% m/m and 3.1% y/y, GDP growth 1.5% q/q with annual 2.1%, manufacturing PMI 53.9, services 56.5, consumer confidence 51.7, retail sales -0.6% m/m. USD IS RAISED FROM +1 TO +2 and the reason is not the single-meeting number, which this file has correctly called noise three times. It is the cumulative pricing and the head-to-head result. CME FedWatch was 44.4% on August 7 and is 60.6% now, and the probability of a hike at September 16, October 28 or December 9 combined has risen from roughly 77% to ABOVE 85% - that is a durable repricing, not a two-point drift. Yesterday PPI confirmed it: headline +0.4% m/m in line but the ANNUAL rate 5.4% against 5.3% expected, with energy accounting for more than three quarters of the rise in final-demand goods and diesel prices up 24.1%. The 10-year yield sits near a 3-year high. Most importantly the dollar beat a HAWKISH ECB head-to-head - the euro fell after a hike with upward-revised projections - which is the cleanest possible evidence of where the marginal dollar is going. Warsh at Jackson Hole on August 28 said the predominant focus should be on prices and, for the first time, that inflation must reach 2% at sufficient speed; TE's July-minutes summary has officials concerned about persistent inflation, several judging conditions possibly not restrictive enough, and a small group wanting an immediate hike. The DISCIPLINED counterweight that caps conviction: core PPI came in SOFTER than expected at +0.2% m/m against 0.3%, the headline beat was energy-driven and therefore exactly the kind a central bank can look through, and DXY at 99.029 is still -0.98% on the month. So direction is raised but every dollar-legged symbol stays at LOW-MED until August CPI prints at 12:30Z - consensus 3.4% headline, core +0.4% m/m and 2.4% y/y, market-implied mean 3.38%.

EUR.when: Oct 29 is the next decision - the September 10 hike is delivered, and TE has no forecast beyond it, but Reuters sources report further tightening remains LIKELY and futures keep December alive
EUR.note: Re-verified on TE: deposit facility now 2.50% from 2.25%, main refi 2.65% from 2.40%, marginal lending 2.90%. EUR HOLDS at +1 and the call this file made yesterday was correct in substance and wrong in consequence, which is worth separating carefully. Substance: it said the 25bp carried no information and the NEW STAFF PROJECTIONS were the whole event, with the asymmetry favouring a hawkish revision. That is precisely what landed. The ECB kept 2026 inflation at 3.0% but revised 2027 UP to 2.5% and 2028 to 2.1%, upgraded growth to 0.9% for 2026 and 1.4% for 2027 citing greater-than-expected resilience, left 2028 growth at 1.5%, said the Middle East conflict continues to generate inflation pressures with inflation set to remain well above target for an extended period, and Lagarde stated inflation risks are tilted to the UPSIDE while growth risks are to the downside, reiterating meeting-by-meeting. Reuters then reported ECB sources saying further tightening remains likely. Consequence: the euro FELL, to 1.16116 from 1.16318, because US PPI beat on the annual and the dollar recovered. The lesson is that a hawkish ECB is no longer enough to own the euro against the dollar - it is only enough to own it against sterling and the kiwi. That is why EUR stays at +1 rather than rising, and why EUR/USD is now a LOW-MED SHORT rather than a range. The terms-of-trade tax has also migrated: German gas jumped 3.41% in a session to 83.14 euros per MWh and is +38.65% on the month, the worst in G10, with EU gas at 80.57 and +31.82%, so the euro area is now carrying the single worst energy exposure on the board. TE macro re-verified: Q2 GDP +0.6% q/q and 1.2% y/y, unemployment 6.4%, August HICP 3.3% with MoM +0.4% and core 2.4%, manufacturing PMI 52.7 from 51.9, services 51.6 from 51.7, wage growth 3.4%, and retail sales -0.6% m/m - the sharpest decline in over a year, which is the genuine soft spot. Own EUR against the kiwi and, with less conviction now, sterling.

GBP.when: Sept 17, 11:00Z - TE carries a 0/9 vote-cut consensus and a 3.75% forecast, unchanged by today's growth beat
GBP.note: Bank Rate re-verified on TE at 3.75%, held 6-3 on July 30 with three members voting for 4.00%. GBP IS UPGRADED FROM MINUS 1 TO ZERO and this file should state plainly that it is honouring an invalidation trigger it wrote itself. Yesterday it said the short was invalidated by a hard upside surprise in monthly GDP at 06:00Z. July GDP printed +0.4% m/m against 0.0% expected, accelerating from 0.3% in June and no growth in May, with services +0.4%, production +0.2% and construction +0.1%, annual growth 1.6% in July, 0.4% over the three months to July and an eighth consecutive three-month period of expansion. That is the growth leg of the weak-sterling thesis broken. A SECOND leg broke in the same session and it is the one this file has led with for three days: sterling is no longer the worst energy exposure in G10. German gas is 83.14 euros per MWh and +38.65% on the month after a 3.41% session jump, while UK gas at 201.52 pence per therm is +34.03% and actually FELL 1.73% today. The relative argument has inverted. What stops the upgrade going any further than zero is unchanged and still real: the Bank will not move on September 17 with a 0/9 TE vote-cut consensus and cannot ease into an October Ofgem cap rise either, borrowing costs remain the highest of any G10 developed nation, July government borrowing was 69% above the prior year, and the yield advantage is a risk premium rather than carry. TE re-verified: CPI 2.9% with core 2.6% and MoM 0.3%, Q2 GDP 0.4% q/q with annual 1.2%, unemployment 4.9%, employment change +83k from +147k, claimant count -11k, wage growth 4.1% from 4.4%, manufacturing PMI 51.7, services 52.5, consumer confidence -14 from -17 and improving, retail sales +1.6% y/y. Consequences for the board: GBP/USD goes to RANGE, GBP/AUD goes to RANGE, EUR/GBP is cut to MEDIUM, GBP/CAD and GBP/CHF are cut to LOW-MED, GBP/JPY is cut to MEDIUM, and GBP/NZD flips from RANGE to a LOW-MED LONG. Sterling is now a neutral currency, not a short.

JPY.when: Sept 18, 03:00Z - 97% of 68 economists in the September 1-8 Reuters poll expect 1.25%, up from 57% in the prior survey, and TE carries consensus AND forecast at 1.25%
JPY.note: Policy rate re-verified on TE at 1.00%, the highest since September 1995, held July 31 by 8-1 with Takata dissenting for 1.25%. JPY HOLDS at +3 and the case got materially STRONGER overnight rather than merely holding. The September 1-8 Reuters poll is the new anchor: all but two of 68 economists, 97%, expect a hike on September 18 against 57% in the previous survey - a 40-point jump in consensus inside a month. More than a third, 24 of 66, expect a FOLLOW-UP to 1.50% in October or December, roughly double August's share. 89% of analysts, 57 of 64, see the policy rate at 1.50% or higher by end-March against 65% last month, and around 62% see 1.75% or higher by end-Q2 2027, three months earlier than August's poll implied. And 82% said the joint US-Japan yen-buying intervention and Treasury Secretary Bessent's remarks on BoJ policy have significantly or somewhat LOWERED the political barrier to hikes - which is the structural point, because it means the MoF is no longer a brake on yen strength. The rhetoric matches: Takata urged a nimble, data-dependent approach warning inflation is edging toward 2% and overheating risks are RISING, Masu said on September 10 that the Bank will continue raising as underlying inflation nears 2% and named Iran-driven fuel and chemical costs, distribution and food costs, yen pass-through and AI demand as persistent pressures, and Ueda hinted at a September move on September 2. Underneath: final Q2 GDP +0.4% q/q with annualised 1.4%, Reuters Tankan 21 from 18, average cash earnings +4.7% y/y and the fastest since 1997, real wages positive for a seventh month, current account PLUS 2,989bn yen, retail sales +2.4% m/m and +4.0% y/y. The one honest caveat remains TE's July-meeting summary: the BoJ CUT its FY2026 inflation forecast to 2.5% from 2.8% on government energy relief while raising FY2026 GDP to 0.6%, FY2027 inflation to 2.4% and growth to 0.8%. TE macro re-verified: CPI 1.9% with core 1.8% and MoM 0.4%, jobless rate 2.4%, GDP 0.4% q/q and 0.7% y/y, business confidence 22, manufacturing PMI 54.9, services 52.5, consumer confidence 35.5. USD/JPY 154.028, -0.26% today and -3.38% on the month, still the largest monthly move of any major.

AUD.when: Sept 29, 04:30Z - TE carries consensus AND forecast at 4.35%, a HOLD, which is the point: the rate leg is a level rather than a catalyst
AUD.note: Cash rate re-verified on TE at 4.35%, the G10 high, held August 11. AUD IS CUT FROM +2 TO +1 and the reasoning needs to be exact because this file held the score yesterday while explicitly removing the commodity argument from under it. Yesterday's stated trigger was a second consecutive soft copper session COMBINED WITH another weak domestic print. Only half of that landed - copper had its second soft session but there was no new weak Australian data today - so this is a one-notch cut, not a collapse, and it stops at +1 rather than going neutral. What forces it is that the commodity leg has gone from weakened to NEGATIVE: copper is 6.5049 USD per pound with its MONTHLY return now -1.42%, having been +1.87% yesterday and +2.90% on the week two days ago, and TE itself now headlines copper holding its decline as tariff fears ease, which is the front-running bid coming out. Silver is -1.87% monthly and gold -1.11%; the entire complex AUD used to lean on is negative. The price confirms: AUD/USD is 0.71719, down 0.44% on the WEEK with its monthly gain cut from +2.12% to +1.56%. And the remaining leg is static - TE carries consensus and forecast at 4.35% for September 29, meaning the market is not being offered a catalyst, only a level. What still supports +1: the G10-high 4.35% cash rate; Melbourne Institute inflation expectations unchanged at 4.9% in September; trimmed mean stuck at 3.6% with headline CPI 3.5% and a July MoM of +1.0%; GDP annual 2.1%, above the RBA estimated 2% speed limit; and the August minutes judging inflation TOO HIGH with excess demand persistent, staff seeing target only by late 2027 with risks skewed upward, and Middle East oil listed FIRST among hike arguments - that argument is stronger with WTI above 100. The honest counterweight is unchanged: Westpac consumer confidence 84.4 after a 5.2% monthly fall, NAB business confidence MINUS 8 from MINUS 6, unemployment 4.5% from 4.4%, employment change -15,827 in July, wage growth only 3.2%. TE re-verified manufacturing PMI 52 and services 53.2. AUD/NZD 1.2297.

NZD.when: Oct 28, 01:00Z is a pause on TE's own calendar; TE forecasts the next 25bp only on Dec 9, to 3.00%
NZD.note: OCR re-verified on TE at 2.75% after the September 2 hike from 2.50%. NZD HOLDS at MINUS 1 and the +0.61% bounce to 0.58325 today does not change it - this file made exactly that mistake on Monday, reported a rebound, withdrew it on Tuesday as a one-session artefact, and the monthly numbers settled the argument. The kiwi is -0.85% on the WEEK and -0.49% on the month, still the ONLY major with a negative monthly return against the dollar. The leg that justifies MINUS 1 has never depended on China: it is a central bank that raised to 2.75% and then declined to validate the next step. TE's own summary of the September 2 decision reads as a bank explaining a hike in the past tense - gradually removing stimulus, annual inflation at 4.1% attributed LARGELY to higher fuel prices from the Middle East conflict, core inflation, wage growth and expectations all judged consistent with a return to the 1-3% band by mid-2027, and household spending weighed down by weak income growth, job insecurity and flat house prices. ANZ reads the statement as not pointing to an October increase, with the language around future decisions deliberately vague and highly conditional, which is why wholesale rates and the kiwi both FELL after a hike. A central bank that hikes and then refuses to guide does not get paid for its carry. TE carries October 28 unchanged with the next 25bp only on December 9. The second-derivative data is still the worst in G10 and got worse again: manufacturing PMI 53.1 from 54.3, having been 60.1 two prints ago; business confidence 53.7 from 56.1; consumer confidence 80.4 from 94.7, a 14-point collapse; unemployment 5.6% from 5.4%, the highest since Q3 2015; services PMI 50.6, barely expanding; retail sales -0.5% m/m; wage growth only 2.1%. Q2 CPI 4.1% from 3.1% and GDP 0.8% q/q with annual 1.5%. It stays at MINUS 1 rather than MINUS 2 only because a majority of MPC members still see upside inflation risks and TE does forecast the December hike.

CAD.when: Oct 28 with the MPR - held for a seventh straight meeting on Sept 2; watch the BoC Summary of Deliberations on Sept 16 at 17:30Z for the internal split
CAD.note: Policy rate re-verified on TE at 2.25%, held September 2. CAD HOLDS at +1 and the broken oil beta is now in its third session, though with one mitigating detail worth adding. Brent is 105.972 and WTI 100.939 - crude has BROKEN 100 dollars with monthly gains of +19.39% and +21.39%, the strongest terms-of-trade impulse of the entire cycle - and USD/CAD is 1.38394, up another 0.05% today. The loonie is not being paid in anything like proportion. geopolitics: The war is now 195 days old and the transmission into FX has narrowed to a single channel, energy, while everything else that used to respond has stopped. The United States is running an explicit tanker-for-tanker policy approved by President Trump: it has sunk or permanently disabled Iranian tankers in the Gulf of Oman and near Kharg Island after Iranian ballistic missiles were fired toward a US carrier and destroyer, and Iran has retaliated against merchant shipping on a large scale - 10 vessels near the Strait of Hormuz in the biggest declared wave of tit-for-tat shipping attacks since the war began, a fatal attack on the bulk carrier Minoan Dignity, the seizure of the tanker Amara, and a missile strike on the Al-Azraq base in Jordan. Iran has declared a restricted maritime area running from Chabahar into parts of the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea, water that lies largely outside the Strait and outside Iranian territorial waters - a claim of jurisdiction enforced by fire rather than by law. Tehran says it is ready for a more intense conflict and will escalate further if US strikes on Iranian territory continue, and President Trump has said the conflict will not end before the November midterms, which removes the near-term de-escalation scenario from the base case. The price response is concentrated and extreme: WTI has BROKEN 100 dollars at 100.939 with a monthly gain of +21.39%, Brent is 105.972 at +19.39%, Urals jumped 8.31% in a single session to 103.70 and is +26.66% monthly, heating oil is +18.06%, coking coal +23.98%, LNG JKM +17.13%, and the European gas complex remains the worst-affected with German gas now the G10 leader at 83.14 euros per MWh and +38.65% monthly after a 3.41% session jump, EU gas at 80.57 and +31.82%, and UK gas at 201.52 pence and +34.03%. Equities have started to register it - the S&P fell 0.48%, the Dow 0.77% and the Nasdaq 0.64% as oil cleared 100, and the Sensex slid to a three-month low. What has NOT happened is any haven bid at all, and today that failure is complete rather than partial: gold at 4,358.18, silver at 64.153 and copper at 6.5049 are ALL negative on the month, and the Swiss franc actually WEAKENED 0.36% during the most violent week of the war. The mechanism is US real rates - PPI beat on the annual at 5.4%, CME FedWatch is 60.6% for September 16 with 2026 hike odds above 85%, and the 10-year sits near a 3-year high - so the discount rate on every non-yielding asset is rising faster than the war can bid it. The FX read follows exactly: own the war through USOIL, where the premium actually accrues, and short GER40, where the energy tax lands on an index that cannot pass it through and where Germany now carries the worst gas exposure in the G10. Do NOT own it through CAD, which has ignored Brent at 106 for three sessions; do NOT own it through gold, silver, copper or the franc, all of which have now failed the same test. The one currency still paying is the yen, and it is paying for a reason only loosely connected to the war: 97% of economists now expect the Bank of Japan to hike on September 18, and the political barrier to yen strength has fallen rather than risen. De-escalation is the main risk to USOIL, to the GER40 short, and to the euro-area energy tax; it would do comparatively little to the yen trade, which is why the yen remains the cleanest expression on the board.
